topic: Sentence-level citation grounding for long-document question answering

selected_papers.title: SpanCite: Sentence-Level Citation Grounding for Long-Document QA
selected_papers.abstract: We propose SpanCite, a decoding-time constraint that requires each generated sentence to be traceable to a specific source span before it is emitted. On a long-document QA benchmark, SpanCite reduces the rate of unsupported claims in generated answers, at the cost of a small added latency overhead from the constrained decoding step. All experiments use English-language documents.

executive_summary.content: This review covers SpanCite, a decoding-time method for keeping generated sentences traceable to their source passages in long-document question answering.

introduction_scope.content: This review covers exactly one paper, SpanCite, chosen for its narrow, well-specified mechanism: a per-sentence traceability constraint applied during decoding. No broader survey of grounding methods is attempted.

thematic_findings.content: SpanCite's central finding is that constraining decoding to require sentence-level traceability reduces the rate of unsupported claims on a long-document QA benchmark [1].

methodology_landscape.content: The constraint is checked at each sentence boundary: a candidate sentence must be traceable to a specific retrieved span before it is emitted, or generation is redirected [1].

contradictions_open_debates.content: With only one paper in scope, there is no cross-paper contradiction to report.

gap_analysis.content: SpanCite's evaluation is limited to English-language documents, and its abstract does not report the constrained decoding step's latency cost in absolute terms [1].

future_research_directions.content: A concrete next step is measuring SpanCite's constrained-decoding latency in absolute terms, since the paper reports only that some added cost exists [1].

conclusion.content: SpanCite offers a focused, single-mechanism approach to reducing unsupported claims in long-document answers [1].
